sources.title: Eusebius, Life of Constantine I
sources.consultedScope: Opened Book I; checked I.35–38 on campaign against Maxentius. Panegyrical Christian narrative.

sources.title: Eusebius, Life of Constantine II
sources.consultedScope: Opened Book II; checked controversy and correspondence chapters around II.61–73. Does not date the initial dispute precisely.

sources.title: Eusebius, Life of Constantine III
sources.consultedScope: Opened Book III; checked III.25–40 on Jerusalem building program; ideological account.

sources.title: Eusebius, Life of Constantine IV
sources.consultedScope: Opened Book IV; checked IV.8–13, IV.41–47, IV.61–64. Panegyric; date/claims need corroboration.

sources.title: Eusebius, Ecclesiastical History X
sources.consultedScope: Opened Book X and checked X.5 rescript text concerning religious freedom/restoration, reproducing Lactantius.

sources.title: Fordham Sourcebook, “Edict of Milan”
sources.consultedScope: Read editorial note and rescript translation; note identifies Latin version in Lactantius and Greek in Eusebius HE X.5. Not the signed instrument from a Milan archive.

sources.title: Lactantius, De mortibus persecutorum 48 (hosted Latin text)
sources.consultedScope: The URL is present in dossier; it was not directly opened in this audit. Use consulted Fordham/Eusebius X.5 instead.

sources.title: Acts and Synodal Letter of Arles (314), modern source page
sources.consultedScope: Read editorial introduction, canons summary and edition references; not a line-by-line collation of the underlying Latin transcription.

sources.title: First Council of Nicaea: canons and post-council letter
sources.consultedScope: Opened page; checked canon 20 (kneeling posture) and letter paragraph on Easter agreement. Translation page, not manuscript apparatus.

sources.title: Council of Sardica: introduction and canons
sources.consultedScope: Opened page; checked introductory date discussion and selected canons. Page itself notes date/text-history uncertainty; not independent resolution of date.

sources.title: Socrates Scholasticus, Ecclesiastical History II
sources.consultedScope: Opened Book II and checked source framing plus sections relevant to return/exile and later controversies. Fifth-century, pro-Nicene narrative, not contemporary witness.

sources.title: Athanasius, Historia Acephala
sources.consultedScope: Opened short text; checked §I.2 for exact return date 21 October 346. Alexandrian/partisan perspective.

sources.title: Athanasius, Apologia de Fuga
sources.consultedScope: Opened text; checked account of nighttime church raid/escape. Apologetic first-person account; not neutral census of troops.

sources.title: Socrates and Sozomen, Book IV, chapter 1 (CCEL)
sources.consultedScope: Opened passage on Constans/Magnentius and political settlement; older translation/editorial presentation.

sources.title: Ammianus Marcellinus, Res Gestae XXII
sources.consultedScope: Opened XXII.2; checked Julian’s entry into Constantinople and assumption of sole rule. Contemporary pagan historian with his own judgments.

sources.title: Julian, Letter 24 to the Alexandrians
sources.consultedScope: Opened translation; checked expulsion order concerning Athanasius. Imperial polemic, not neutral report of popular opinion.

sources.title: Ammianus Marcellinus, Res Gestae XXV
sources.consultedScope: Opened; checked account of Julian’s wound/death and burial direction near Tarsus; eyewitness historian, precise wound-cause remains disputed.

sources.title: Codex Theodosianus 16.1.2, Edictum de fide catholica
sources.consultedScope: Opened Latin text and editorial header. Supports legal prescription; does not establish uniform enforcement or social conversion.

sources.title: Council of Constantinople I, creed/canons translation
sources.consultedScope: Opened page; checked canon 3 and editorial transmission note. Compiled translation, not contemporary acts/manuscript apparatus.

sources.title: Codex Theodosianus II (Latin Library transcription)
sources.consultedScope: Opened and checked CTh 2.8.1. Website transcription; date/addressee and exception wording checked, not a critical edition.

sources.title: Sozomen, Ecclesiastical History II
sources.consultedScope: Opened/found II.30; checked narrative of Arius’ death. Fifth-century pro-Nicene polemic, with providential framing, not neutral forensic evidence.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Constantine I
sources.consultedScope: Dossier URL was not successfully consulted for this audit; battle chronology remains unverified here.

sources.title: Ammianus Marcellinus, Res Gestae XXII (Chicago-hosted text)
sources.consultedScope: Opened XXII.2; no exact evidence located there for reopening temples/sacrifices.

sources.title: Athanasius, Historia Acephala
sources.consultedScope: See source record above; duplicate URL retained only once in sources.

sources.title: Socrates Scholasticus, Ecclesiastical History I
sources.consultedScope: Opened Book I and checked Antioch-related context; the examined passage is later than the proposed pre-Nicaea synod and does not establish the selection.

episodes.passages: Eusebius VC I.35–38; checked narrative of final advance and Maxentius’ death near Rome; Lactantius 44 not consulted directly in this pass.
episodes.claimENes: Supports a Constantine victory over Maxentius and entry into Rome in Eusebius’ account. / Respalda la victoria de Constantino sobre Majencio y su entrada en Roma según Eusebio.
episodes.limitations: No exact 28 October date established by checked Eusebius passage; victory/bridge details are framed as Christian providence in a panegyric.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Eusebius VC I.35–38 page/find passages; not Lactantius 44.

episodes.passages: Eusebius HE X.5 / Fordham translation of rescript; checked editorial note describing Milan meeting.
episodes.claimENes: Supports a policy agreement attributed to the rulers at Milan, followed by a rescript granting religious freedom. / Apoya un acuerdo político atribuido a los gobernantes en Milán, seguido de un rescripto de libertad religiosa.
episodes.limitations: The “negotiation” phrasing is an inference; surviving text is later rescript, not minutes of a conversation. Lactantius page URL in dossier was not opened.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Fordham note and translated rescript; Eusebius HE X.5 checked.

episodes.passages: Eusebius HE X.5 as reproduced in Fordham; lines on Nicomedia and restitution.
episodes.claimENes: Supports Licinius’ Nicomedian publication of a rescript ordering freedom of worship and restoration of communal property. / Apoya la publicación nicomediense de un rescripto de Licinio que ordena libertad de culto y restitución de bienes comunitarios.
episodes.limitations: The text is not the original Milan instrument; legal order is not proof of uniform practical restitution.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Fordham editorial note and rescript translation; Eusebius HE X.5 checked.

episodes.passages: No exact passage directly consulted for the dossier’s Rome/Ostia hearings; Eusebius HE X.5 mentions a Roman decision only indirectly in the contextual tradition.
episodes.claimENes: A Donatist dispute and episcopal/imperial adjudication are broadly attested by later sources, but this particular source audit does not verify the proposed hearings or location. / Las fuentes posteriores atestiguan en términos generales la disputa donatista y su arbitraje episcopal/imperial, pero esta auditoría no verifica las audiencias ni el lugar propuestos.
episodes.limitations: Dossier URLs (Fourth Century/Optatus) not opened in this pass; Rome/Ostia may conflate distinct hearings. Needs primary passage before treating as established.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: No qualifying exact passage consulted.

episodes.passages: Council of Arles page, introductory lines 16–17 and references to canons 1, 8, 20.
episodes.claimENes: Supports a 314 council convened after the Caecilian/Donatist dispute, with canons addressing Pascha, baptism and episcopal consecration. / Respalda un concilio de 314 convocado tras la disputa de Ceciliano y los donatistas, con cánones sobre Pascua, bautismo y consagraciones episcopales.
episodes.limitations: Page’s narrative introduction is modern editorial framing; it gives 1 August 314, while precise dating derives from scholarly reconstruction. Checked summary, not full canonical text.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Editorial introduction and canon summary only.

episodes.passages: No accessible primary/academic passage opened for Cibalae in this pass; dossier relies on Britannica.
episodes.claimENes: The claimed battle and 317 settlement were not verified in consulted material. / La batalla y el acuerdo de 317 no se verificaron en material consultado.
episodes.limitations: Dating 314 vs 316 is disputed; Britannica URL not consulted. Do not present either year as settled here.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: No qualifying passage consulted.

episodes.passages: Codex Theodosianus 2.8.1 (Constantine to Elpidius; Latin transcription, 3 July 321).
episodes.claimENes: Supports restrictions on judicial business on Sunday, with emancipation/manumission allowed. / Respalda restricciones a la actividad judicial dominical, con excepción para manumisiones.
episodes.limitations: The cited law does not contain the agricultural-work exception; that appears in a different legal context. Replace or remove that claim. Website is a transcription rather than critical edition.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Checked CTh 2.8.1 text and adjacent law; agricultural exception absent here.

episodes.passages: Eusebius VC II.61–64 checked for dispute background and imperial intervention.
episodes.claimENes: Supports a dispute involving Arius and Alexander that drew imperial correspondence and wider church attention in Eusebius’ narrative. / Apoya que la disputa entre Arrio y Alejandro atrajo correspondencia imperial y atención eclesiástica más amplia en el relato de Eusebio.
episodes.limitations: Eusebius’ account is selective and pro-Constantinian; date range 324–325 and the phrase “networks” are editorial synthesis, not an exact dated event.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: VC II.61–64 checked; whole book not read.

episodes.passages: No precise battle passage opened; Eusebius VC II checked generally, Britannica not consulted.
episodes.claimENes: The checked material does not establish Adrianople on 3 July or distinguish this battle from Chrysopolis. / El material consultado no establece Adrianópolis el 3 de julio ni separa esa batalla de Crisópolis.
episodes.limitations: Date and military detail remain unverified in this audit; should retain as conventional only with a better source.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: No exact battle locator found.

episodes.passages: No precise battle passage opened; Eusebius VC II checked generally, Britannica not consulted.
episodes.claimENes: The checked material does not independently verify the 18 September date or Chrysopolis location. / El material consultado no verifica independientemente la fecha del 18 de septiembre ni el lugar de Crisópolis.
episodes.limitations: Do not merge both battles as one event; precise conventional dates need source support.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: No exact battle locator found.

episodes.passages: Socrates HE I.25 checked only for post-Nicaea Antioch context; it does not establish the selected pre-Nicaea suspension claim. Wiley article not consulted.
episodes.claimENes: The proposed pre-Nicaea Antioch synod and suspensions are not confirmed by the passage actually checked. / El sínodo antioqueno previo a Nicea y las suspensiones propuestas no quedan confirmados por el pasaje realmente consultado.
episodes.limitations: Potential confusion with the Antioch synod after Nicaea; specialist article remains unconsulted.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Socrates passage checked, but it does not support this event.

episodes.passages: Nicaea page: canon 20; post-council letter paragraph on Easter (lines 93–95).
episodes.claimENes: Supports council canons including Sunday/Pentecost prayer posture and a reported agreement to celebrate Easter together. / Respalda cánones como la postura de oración en domingo/Pentecostés y un acuerdo comunicado sobre la celebración común de Pascua.
episodes.limitations: Canon 20 is not an Easter-calendar canon. The surviving letter is a post-council report; it does not supply a detailed computational rule or prove uniform compliance.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Canon 20 and letter passage checked, not manuscript history.

episodes.passages: Eusebius VC III.25–40 checked for imperial church-building at Jerusalem.
episodes.claimENes: Supports Constantine’s sponsored construction at Jerusalem, including the church complex associated with the tomb of Jesus in Eusebius’ account. / Respalda el patrocinio de construcciones constantinianas en Jerusalén, incluido el complejo asociado al sepulcro según Eusebio.
episodes.limitations: Eusebius is a Christian panegyrist; source establishes patronage and his identification, not independent proof of the biblical site or the exact dating of each work.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: VC III.25–40 read in relevant sections.

episodes.passages: Chronicon Paschale not directly consulted; Britannica URL not consulted.
episodes.claimENes: Ceremonial dedication of Constantinople in 330 is not independently substantiated by a primary passage checked here. / La dedicación ceremonial de Constantinopla en 330 no queda corroborada aquí por un pasaje primario consultado.
episodes.limitations: 11 May is a conventional date but remains unverified in this audit; avoid implying all construction occurred on dedication day.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: No source passage consulted.

episodes.passages: Eusebius VC IV.8–13 checked: embassy and Constantine’s letter to the Persian king.
episodes.claimENes: Supports Eusebius’ report that Constantine wrote to the Persian king advocating for Christians under his rule. / Respalda el informe de Eusebio de que Constantino escribió al rey persa en defensa de los cristianos de su territorio.
episodes.limitations: Eusebius does not establish the dossier’s c.332–333 date in this passage; identify the recipient as Sapor/Shapur only as Eusebius names him. Panegyrical source, not Persian-side confirmation.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: VC IV.8–13 checked.

episodes.passages: Eusebius VC IV.41–47 checked: Tyre proceedings and Jerusalem dedication (IV.47).
episodes.claimENes: Supports a council at Tyre involving charges against Athanasius and a later dedication of the Jerusalem complex in Eusebius’ account. / Respalda un concilio en Tiro con acusaciones contra Atanasio y una posterior dedicación del complejo jerosolimitano según Eusebio.
episodes.limitations: The source is hostile/panegyrical toward Athanasius; separate the Tyre council from Jerusalem dedication. Chronology is not precise enough to imply immediate sequence without qualification.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: VC IV.41–47 checked.

episodes.passages: Sozomen HE II.30 (New Advent 26022), account of Arius’ death.
episodes.claimENes: Supports a later tradition that Arius died at Constantinople on the eve of a planned readmission. / Respalda una tradición posterior según la cual Arrio murió en Constantinopla la víspera de una readmisión prevista.
episodes.limitations: Sozomen presents the death as providential punishment and explicitly reports hearsay; date 336 is not established by this passage. The cited dossier URL 26023 is Book III and is wrong for II.29.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Chapter 30 lines found/read; polemical account, not contemporary evidence.

episodes.passages: Eusebius VC IV.61–64 checked for baptism and death at Nicomedia.
episodes.claimENes: Supports Constantine’s baptism by Eusebius of Nicomedia and death at Nicomedia in 337 in Eusebius’ account. / Respalda el bautismo por Eusebio de Nicomedia y la muerte de Constantino en Nicomedia en 337 según Eusebio.
episodes.limitations: The narrative is an imperial Christian encomium; day 22 May is not independently verified by the passage checked.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: VC IV.61–64 checked.

episodes.passages: Socrates HE II.1 / II.25 identified as relevant narrative; checked introductory framing and selected passage context.
episodes.claimENes: Supports post-Constantinian imperial succession narrated by Socrates, a fifth-century historian. / Respalda la sucesión imperial posterior a Constantino en el relato del historiador del siglo V Sócrates.
episodes.limitations: Not a contemporary dispatch; exact territorial division and timing need passage-level audit before detailed map/campaign claims.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Book II page opened; limited chapter checks, not all cited sections.

episodes.passages: Sardica canons page: introduction and selected canons; Anastos link not opened.
episodes.claimENes: Supports Sardica’s canons and appellate procedures, but this audit did not verify the claim of distinct east/west sessions from an exact narrative passage. / Respalda los cánones de Sardica y procedimientos de apelación, pero no verifica aquí mediante pasaje narrativo la afirmación de sesiones separadas entre este y oeste.
episodes.limitations: Page’s own date discussion is inconsistent/uncertain (343/344; wider alternatives); avoid a precise date without resolving textual chronology.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Intro and selected canons checked; Anastos not consulted.

episodes.passages: Historia Acephala §I.2; Socrates HE II contextual account.
episodes.claimENes: Supports Athanasius’ return to Alexandria on 21 October 346 after time in Rome/Italy. / Respalda el regreso de Atanasio a Alejandría el 21 de octubre de 346 tras su estancia en Roma e Italia.
episodes.limitations: Athanasius’ chronicle is aligned with his side of the dispute; support from imperial letters is broadly reported, but the exact political motives should not be inferred.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Historia Acephala §I.2 read directly; Socrates page checked as context.

episodes.passages: Socrates/CCEL passage on Constans’ death in Gaul in 350 and Magnentius.
episodes.claimENes: Supports Constans’ death during Magnentius’ usurpation and Magnentius’ control in the West. / Respalda la muerte de Constante durante la usurpación de Magnencio y el control magnenciano de Occidente.
episodes.limitations: Candidate is wrong to say Constantius II became sole emperor in 350; Magnentius remained a rival until defeated in 353. Geographic focus Milan is reception of news, not death site.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Relevant narrative passage opened; source is later ecclesiastical history.

episodes.passages: Athanasius Historia Acephala and Apologia de Fuga checked for February 356 church raid/escape; no evidence for the Milan hearing in this source.
episodes.claimENes: The source supports Athanasius’ account of a nighttime raid and escape at a church in Alexandria, not the Milan synod/hearing in 355. / La fuente respalda el relato de Atanasio sobre una incursión nocturna y su huida en Alejandría, no una audiencia en Milán en 355.
episodes.limitations: Episode has wrong local event/date alignment: Milan hearing and Alexandria raid are distinct episodes. Athanasius is a partisan witness; figures and adversary descriptions require caution.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Relevant short texts checked; narrative scope not neutral.

episodes.passages: Athanasius Historia Acephala / Apologia de Fuga; exact raid account checked.
episodes.claimENes: Supports Athanasius’ report that soldiers entered a church in Alexandria at night and that he escaped. / Respalda el informe de Atanasio de que soldados entraron de noche en una iglesia de Alejandría y él escapó.
episodes.limitations: Potential duplicate with episode 23; source is partisan and the reported troop count is not independently verified. Keep only if the two episodes have distinct historical content.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Relevant sections checked in both short texts.

episodes.passages: Socrates HE II.37 and II.39–40: Ariminum and Seleucia both met in 359, Seleucia divided into factions; the text places Seleucia meeting on 27 September.
episodes.claimENes: Supports the parallel western council at Ariminum and eastern council at Seleucia in 359, with disagreement and factional division. / Respalda los sínodos paralelos de Arímino y Seleucia en 359, con desacuerdo y división en facciones.
episodes.limitations: Socrates is a fifth-century pro-Nicene narrator. The selected page supports that these were separate synods, not that they pursued an identical formula or produced a single outcome.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Socrates HE II.37 and II.39–40 checked via find excerpts; not the entire book.

episodes.passages: Ammianus XXII.2 §1 checked for Julian’s entry into Constantinople and sole rule.
episodes.claimENes: Supports Julian entering Constantinople after Constantius’ death and becoming sole ruler. / Respalda la entrada de Juliano en Constantinopla tras la muerte de Constancio y su gobierno único.
episodes.limitations: This passage does not support reopening temples/restoring sacrifices; that needs a separate exact source. Ammianus is an admiring pagan narrator.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: XXII.2 §1 checked; no temple-policy passage located.

episodes.passages: Julian Letter 24 checked for order that Athanasius leave Alexandria; Ammianus XXV checked for death during Persian campaign.
episodes.claimENes: Supports Julian ordering Athanasius out of Alexandria and Ammianus’ account of Julian’s fatal wound/death on the Persian campaign, near the Tigris/Mesopotamian theater. / Respalda la orden de expulsión de Atanasio y el relato de Amiano sobre la herida mortal y muerte de Juliano durante la campaña persa, en el teatro mesopotámico.
episodes.limitations: Julian’s letter is polemical; exact wound cause and killer are uncertain. The Persian campaign/death is not a local Alexandria event—present as reported news, not on-map action.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Julian Letter 24 and Ammianus XXV relevant lines checked.

episodes.passages: CTh 16.1.2 Latin text and editorial heading checked.
episodes.claimENes: Supports an imperial law prescribing the faith associated with Damasus and Peter for inhabitants of Constantinople and labeling dissenting groups as heretics. / Respalda una ley imperial que prescribe la fe asociada con Dámaso y Pedro para los habitantes de Constantinopla y califica de herejes a grupos disidentes.
episodes.limitations: The constitution is addressed to the people of Constantinople though issued at Thessalonica; it does not prove uniform enforcement, conversion, or universal application. Header date/location should be checked in a critical edition if exact day matters.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Latin text and page heading read.

episodes.passages: Council of Constantinople I page, canon 3 and editorial transmission note.
episodes.claimENes: Supports canon 3’s honor ranking of Constantinople after Rome because it is New Rome. / Respalda el rango honorífico de Constantinopla después de Roma en el canon 3, por ser Nueva Roma.
episodes.limitations: Canon is about precedence/honor, not a modern Catholic/Orthodox split or unrestricted jurisdiction. Creed text transmission is separate; page is a translation/compilation.
episodes.coverageActuallyRead: Canon 3 and editorial note checked; not manuscript apparatus.
